root_idea.summary: The root centers on acquiring, possessing, and having an abundance of wealth.
root_idea.development: The lexical range develops from taking or acquiring wealth to wealth as possessed property. The noun is described as extending from gold and silver to acquired substantial possessions, with livestock a prominent pastoral application.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular dictionary citation form مَال, encompassing the Quranic singular and plural occurrences.

senses.definition: Property or wealth: things acquired and possessed.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for individual or collective possessions, including substantial goods. Depending on context, it may be rendered as wealth, property, or capital; the Quranic group includes both مَال and its plural أَمْوَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels, sheep, or goats kept as pastoral wealth; herds or flocks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral application, especially for the livestock constituting the wealth of desert people.
The plural أَمْوَالٌ is attested for this technical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wealthy man, or a man possessing wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction used in place of ذُو مَالٍ.
Form V verb describing the attainment of abundant wealth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of or relating to property or wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective relating something to مال in the sense of property or wealth.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form V lexical meaning represented under the derived verb.
General property/wealth meaning and the prominent livestock application are represented.

cautions: The single QAC form group combines singular مَال and plural أَمْوَال; the public headword uses the singular citation form. English renderings such as “wealth,” “property,” and “capital” are contextual realizations of the same Quranic noun.
